This morning’s edition of the paper adds that the Portuguese star appeals because of his versatility, too. He can play as a deeper-lying midfield player – as he did under Ruben Amorim at Old Trafford – as a box-to-box player and as an attacking midfielder.

The latter is perhaps his preferred role, especially now that he is into his 30s. Interestingly, Amorim has switched from being locked into the 3-4-2-1 seen at United to now using more of a 4-2-3-1 in possession, so in theory there could be an ideal role waiting for Fernandes.

  • The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 20 Nov 2026 22:07.

BB Erzurumspor will be looking to end their recent losing run when they welcome Goztepe to Kazim Karabekir Stadium on Sunday afternoon.

The hosts sit 12th in the Turkish Super Lig standings after 11 matches, while the visitors occupy 10th place and will be hoping to bounce back from their latest defeat to maintain their push towards the upper half of the table.

Erzurumspor had enjoyed an encouraging spell before their recent setbacks, recording victories over Eyupspor and Gaziantep, as well as a draw with Alanyaspor and a win against Samsunspor, to put together a four-game unbeaten run and move away from the lower reaches of the standings.

However, their momentum was checked when they suffered a 3-1 home defeat against Corum before losing 2-1 away to Caykur Rizespor in their most recent league outing before the international break.

Erzurumspor took the lead against Rizespor through Ibrahim Diabate, but they were unable to hold on to their advantage as the hosts turned the contest around, leaving Serkan Ozbalta's side with consecutive defeats after they had collected 10 points from their preceding four matches.

Despite those setbacks, the hosts will be encouraged by their home performances this season, having beaten Konyaspor, Eyupspor and Samsunspor while suffering defeats against Galatasaray and Corum, the latter being their most recent appearance in front of their supporters.

They will be keen to rediscover the defensive organisation that helped them secure those three victories without conceding, particularly against a Goztepe side that has demonstrated considerable attacking quality in recent weeks.

This will be the fifth Super Lig meeting between the sides, with Erzurumspor picking up two wins, drawing one and losing one of the previous four, although they have lost their last two encounters against the visitors, one in the Turkish Cup and the other in the second division.

Goztepe, meanwhile, had been enjoying an impressive run of results before their latest setback, winning four consecutive league matches as part of a six-game unbeaten streak to establish themselves in the top half of the table.

Stanimir Stoilov's side began that sequence with a 4-0 away victory over Eyupspor before recording a 2-1 win against Kocaelispor and a 2-0 home triumph over Corum.

The visitors then produced one of their most impressive performances of the campaign by defeating Fenerbahce 2-1 away from home.

However, their winning streak came to an end just before the break when they suffered a 2-1 home defeat against Istanbul Basaksehir, with Juan finding the net but the hosts ultimately unable to prevent their opponents from taking all three points.

Goztepe nevertheless have an away unbeaten run to protect, with Goz Goz having gone four games without defeat on the road, winning their last three and drawing the other.

BB Erzurumspor Turkish Super Lig form:.

Goztepe SK Turkish Super Lig form:.

Erzurumspor are not expected to have any major suspension concerns heading into the match, although there have been conflicting reports regarding the fitness of several players, including Gyrano Kerk and Festy Ebosele, who are both included in some predicted lineups despite being listed as injury concerns elsewhere.

Ibrahim Diabate is expected to retain his place in attack after scoring in the recent defeat against Rizespor, while Miguel Cardoso, Brandon Baiye and Elisha Owusu are likely to feature in midfield as the hosts look to improve their attacking output.

Goztepe could be without Furkan Bayir and Ogun Bayrak, who have both been reported as injury doubts, while Ibrahim Sabra is continuing his recovery from an ankle injury after returning to training.

Juan is expected to lead the visitors' attacking line alongside Janderson, with Alexis Antunes likely to operate behind the front two as Goz Goz look to maintain their attacking threat.

BB Erzurumspor possible starting lineup:.

Taskiran; Ebosele, Ovacikli, Gerxhaliu, Mujakic, Giorbelidze; Kerk, Owusu, Baiye, Cardoso; Diabate.

Goztepe SK possible starting lineup:.

Ozcimen; Bokele, Godoi, Altikardes; Kurtulan, Rhaldney, Miroshi, Akonnor; Antunes; Juan, Janderson.

Erzurumspor will be eager to take advantage of their home support after consecutive defeats, but Goztepe have demonstrated greater attacking consistency in recent weeks, and we expect Stoilov's side to return to winning ways with a narrow victory.

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:33 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 04:07 EST, 20 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to reset the culture at Manchester United as he lifted the lid on being in the stands in 1999 to see the club's greatest triumph.

Pochettino was officially appointed as United's latest head coach on Wednesday and took charge of training for the first time on Thursday.

The Argentine was pictured greeting his newly introduced squad, with several stars having returned from international duty, before attentions turned to preparing the Red Devils for Sunday's trip to Anfield.

Pochettino also addressed the club's internal media team for the first time, outlining how he aims to drag this underperforming squad up the table.

'The culture is the most notable,' Pochettino explained.

'Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

Mauricio Pochettino took Man United first team training for the first time on Thursday.

Matheus Cunha and Lisandro Martinez were among those to report back after international duty.

Man United will hope to hit the ground running under Pochettino when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

'We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us to be close to winning every single game.'.

Recent findings suggest that 'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure.'.

Pochettino's determination to be the man to bring winning football back to Old Trafford is in large part due to one of his founding memories of the club back in 1999 when he was a player at Espanyol.

Alongside his now trusted goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez, Pochettino was at the Nou Camp to see United clinch the Champions League, thus sealing a famous Treble, against Bayern Munich.

'In 1999, I was in Barcelona for that final. That was an iconic final,' he added.

'Toni Jimenez [was there] too. We were shouting for Manchester United from there. I was so excited to see Manchester United.

'This [is the] type of game that you stay sitting in your place [for] and you're so excited because you are watching the game. That was an amazing game.

'And then what happened in the end... it's like it's impossible not to empathise with that team, no?

'That was an amazing memory that made me pay more attention to United, to [Sir Alex] Ferguson and the players that were there, that are all legends.'.

That level of success feels a lifetime away from the current squad, which emerges from the international break for a trip to face bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield slumped 18th in the Premier League.

Pochettino wants to focus on the potential of his Man United squad, rather than their current Premier League plight.

Pochettino is determined to shift the culture at Manchester United back to winning.

The Argentine head coach was in the stands in Barcelona cheering for United back in 1999.

While there are those who may be daunted trying to turn around the ship which sunk so far it cost Michael Carrick his job, Pochettino wants to focus on potential, rather than the present.

Industry observers note that 'It's a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club,' a defiant Pochettino added.

Recent findings suggest that 'Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it's a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

'The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most vital thing and that is our priority now – it's to work with them and try to take the pressure [off].

It has been revealed that 'Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it's too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back.

'When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

According to recent reports, 'That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff - we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

'I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.'.

Pochettino touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning after his overnight flight.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

In a recent development, pochettino knows that time is not on his side ahead of an upcoming week that sees United travel to face Liverpool on Sunday, followed by a Champions League trip to face Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday. The week is rounded out by a home match a week on Saturday against Brentford.

The Argentine head coach touched down in Manchester on Wednesday morning, taking a private jet straight after the final whistle of United States versus Haiti in Cincinnati.

Industry observers note that from there he immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff, including Tom Heaton, Luke Shaw, Mason Mount and Bruno Fernandes. It is understood he left a good first impression on the players.

And yet, in spite of such a packed schedule, which saw him leave Carrington very late at night on Wednesday and reappear bright and early on Thursday for training, Pochettino is raring to go and is eager for his players to head to Anfield on Sunday convinced they can win.

According to recent reports, 'I have plenty of energy. It's a privilege to be head coach of Manchester United,' he said.

In a recent development, 'And we are not wasting time. We need to be ready to compete on Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that 'Now it's not time to think about rest, it's not time to think about sleep. It's about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.'.

#72058. Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 44m • 📚 Deep Dive (8869 w)

Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8869 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4.
  • In a recent development, unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4.
  • The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies1,2,3,4. Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases2,5,6. However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space7,8,9,10,11,12), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

In a recent development, unlike covalently bonded heterostructures, van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by the delicate balance between van der Waals forces, Coulomb interactions and the local strain1,2,3,4. Depending on the relative weight of those energy terms, many different phenomena have been observed: the Hofstadter butterfly depending mainly on the van der Waals coupling13,14,15, commensurate–incommensurate phase transitions driven by van der Waals–strain competition5,6 and flat-band formation that probably involves all three contributions and facilitates superconductivity and correlated insulating phase 16,17,18.

The particular stacking configuration and the atomic registry between neighbouring layers are likewise controlled by the balance of those energies. Varying their relative contributions can switch the system between different atomic arrangements, resulting in structural phase transitions potentially accompanied by the emergence of latest electronic phases. This points to a rich underlying phase diagram. Yet experimental platforms that allow controlled exploration of this phase space so far have been lacking.

Sources indicate that here we demonstrate that, by careful tuning of the balance between these competing interactions in a three-layer van der Waals heterostructure, we can reach simultaneous structural and electronic phase transitions, controlled through layer charging, magnetic field or temperature variation. We engineer these transitions in a heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hBN and mhBN on either side: mhBN/graphene/hBN. In such heterostructures, strain is greatly enhanced because mhBN, unlike its bulk counterpart, is free to contract and corrugate (the strain amplitude is controlled by the number of hBN layers), leading to strongly enhanced surface reconstruction19,20,21. The van der Waals interaction of this system is likewise enhanced by the double alignment and can be tuned by gate-charging the graphene layer.

In such heterostructure devices, the structural phase transition reveals itself through an abrupt, global and reversible switch of the stacking configuration, which entails a change of symmetry (analogous to the Bernal-to-rhombohedral transition in graphite22,23,24,25) and results in distinct reconstruction modes observed directly by scanning tunnelling microscopy (STM). It is accompanied by a unique electronic phase transition: switching between p-doping and n-doping of graphene. Unlike conventional doping, the doping levels before and after the phase transition are discrete rather than continuous in nature, always taking an integer or ‘quantized’ value corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons per moiré unit cell, which we hereafter term integer doping. We attribute this integer doping to electrons (holes) being trapped in the strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (PLLs), formed by the strong moiré surface reconstruction; these localized states constitute flat bands in k-space, as predicted theoretically7,8,9,10,11 and confirmed by STM measurements12. The structural transition alters the atomic arrangement, modifying both the strain and scalar-potential landscapes. In reciprocal space, we interpret this as switching the hybridization of these flat bands between the valence band (AB phase) and the conduction band (AA phase), inverting the sign of the integer doping.

Our heterostructure consists of monolayer graphene that is double-aligned, on one side to hBN and on the other side to mhBN (refs. 19,20). Unlike single alignment, such double-aligned ‘sandwich’ heterostructures can exhibit either parallel or antiparallel orientations corresponding to the 0° and 180° angle alignment between the top and bottom hBN (refs. 2,19,26). The results obtained on both types of device are similar, so in the main text, we focus on the parallel orientation, presenting the analysis for the antiparallel orientation in Supplementary Information Sections 20, 23, 26 and 28 (Supplementary Figs. 30, 41 and 42).

In a recent development, for either orientation, two energetically competing stacking configurations exist (Fig. 1c,d), which are interconvertible by sliding the mhBN by one interatomic distance relative to the bulk hBN (detailed explanation and simple schematics in Supplementary Information Section 21; Supplementary Figs. 31 and 32). This is analogous to the transition between ABC (rhombohedral) and ABA (Bernal) trilayer graphene, in which a small shift of one of the layers leads to strong reconfigurations of the electronic bands22,23,24,25.

a, Schematic representation of the full phase diagram formed in our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN system. External parameters (such as carrier density n, magnetic field B and temperature T) define one coordinate axis, whereas the intrinsic stacking order of the sandwich heterostructure defines the other. Two local energy minima exist corresponding to AA and AB stacking configurations, with their dominant stackings shown in c and d, respectively. Blue and red arrows indicate transitions between these configurations; solid arrows denote states realized under continuous tuning of external parameters, whereas dashed arrows mark the abrupt structural phase transition, matching the solid and dashed lines in the experiments shown in Fig. 3a–c. b, Moiré-induced corrugation observed in a double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN device, measured at room temperature by AFM. Inset shows the corrugation profile along the light blue line. Phonon squeezing reduces corrugation at low temperatures. The unit cell outlined in black matches that in g. c,d, Schematic illustrations of the competing sandwich configurations at double-aligned interfaces: AB (c) and AA (d) stacking configurations. e–h, MD simulations of strain distributions. Panels g and h show our double-aligned mhBN/graphene/hBN configurations with AB and AA stacking configurations, respectively, and panels e and f show reference calculations for double-aligned hBN/graphene/hBN configurations. Comparison highlights the notable role of mhBN on strain enhancement, leading to much stronger reconstruction patterns—triangular and hexagonal reconstructions, respectively. Dashed circles indicate vertices of domains arising from these two reconstruction types, on which strain-induced PLLs develop, as shown on the right. The yellow-to-orange gradient bar indicates increasing strain amplitude. i, The theoretical calculated corrugation of the graphene–hBN interface as a function of the twist angle.

According to recent reports, unlike previous studies that apply a mechanical tool such as an atomic force microscope or scanning tunnelling microscope tip to locally ‘iron’ the sample to toggle the stacking configurations in confined regions of sample27,28, our system allows global, reversible switching between the two stacking states simply by tuning external parameters, including carrier density n, magnetic field B or temperature T. Such all-electronic control is far better suited to device integration and to triggering new phenomena in transport measurements. The schematic in Fig. 1a illustrates the full phase diagram defined by these external parameters and the intrinsic stacking order, in which the two local minima correspond to the competing AB and AA stacking configurations. Accompanying this switch, the moiré-induced strain distribution and thus the lattice reconstruction changes from triangular to hexagonal patterns (Fig. 1e–h; see also the STM images in Fig. 5a,b), ultimately leading to different pseudomagnetic field (PMF) distributions2,29 (Fig. 5e,f) and different band reconfigurations (Fig. 5g–j).

We emphasize that the mhBN is essential for enhancing such lattice reconstruction of graphene, as mhBN itself can accommodate a finite amount of strain, allowing both layers (mhBN and graphene) to undergo very strong relaxation. The molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, comparing mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1g,h) and hBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 1e,f) heterostructures, clearly demonstrate that the presence of mhBN greatly amplifies the periodic strain induced by moiré reconstruction. The experimental evidence, including room-temperature atomic force microscopy (AFM) measurement of the corrugation (Fig. 1b) and the same measurement with varying hBN layer numbers (1–4 layers; Supplementary Information Section 13; Supplementary Fig. 19) and their corresponding transport properties, is presented in Supplementary Information Section 4. As well as mhBN, alignment also markedly influences the strain, as shown by the calculated corrugation with respect to the twist angle in Fig. 1i.

Two types of transport device are discussed in the main text: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN (Fig. 2a) and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN (Fig. 2b). In the former, the mhBN–hBN interface is intentionally misaligned by 15° to achieve superlubricity, preserving the double-aligned sandwich structure. The two architectures are complementary: the dual-gated capped devices enable higher carrier concentrations and allow the roles of doping and the displacement field to be disentangled (Supplementary Information Section 8), whereas the non-capped mhBN/graphene/hBN structure develops stronger reconstruction, in particular the out-of-plane corrugation at the graphene–mhBN interface (Supplementary Information Section 30).

Sources indicate that a, Schematic of the transport device with hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN heterostructure (inset) in a dual-graphite gate configuration. b, Schematic of the mhBN/graphene/hBN transport device. The unencapsulated mhBN enables AFM measurement. Inset, AFM image of the device (bottom right) and its fast Fourier transform (FFT). The FFT confirms the double alignment and gives the periods of both superlattices, which agree well with those derived from the transport measurement in d. Scale bar, 50 nm. c,d, Longitudinal resistance Rxx of the states before (blue) and after (red) the transition in the device types in a and b, measured at T = 1.6 K. The neutrality point, labelled ‘NP’, shifts from no doping to n-doping (device in a) and from p-doping to n-doping (device in b) on transition. The top axis marks doping levels corresponding to integer multiples of electrons or holes per moiré unit cell. The doping shift relative to zero is denoted by Δnint, in which ‘int’ signifies intrinsic doping (in contrast to external doping by gate). For the device in a, the bottom axis (Vdual D = 0) is defined such that both Vtg and Vbg are simultaneously tuned to vary carrier density while maintaining zero displacement field in graphene. By contrast, the device in b has only back gate, so its bottom axis is represented by Vbg. e,f, The doping levels of other same-structured devices with different periods of moiré plaquette λm before (blue dots) and after (red dots) transition. The details of all samples are presented in Supplementary Information Section 3 and Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6. The doping levels of all samples, before and after the transition, are located at integer multiples of electrons per moiré unit cell, with the percentage deviation from ideal integer multiples (Δnint − Nn0)/Nn0 shown by bar graphs at the corresponding positions, in which Δnint − Nn0 is the deviation from the nearest integer multiple N (if N is 0, then we choose the denominator Nn0 = n0).

For both architectures, double alignment of graphene to the hBN crystals on both sides was confirmed by AFM, Raman and transport measurements (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 2). We emphasize that both the double alignment and the presence of mhBN are crucial for the effects we observe, as corroborated by seven types of reference device, none of which exhibit the transition (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4; Supplementary Figs. 7 and 8).

First, let us examine the initial-state transfer curves (blue) of the two device types in Fig. 2c,d. In the hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN sample, the neutrality point of graphene remains at zero doping, whereas the mhBN/graphene/hBN structure exhibits p-doping. Notably, this p-doping level closely approximates 2n0 (n0 corresponds to doping of one charge carrier per moiré plaquette). In 8 of 9 unencapsulated mhBN/graphene/hBN devices (blue dots in Fig. 2f), the p-doping is quantized at Nn0 (N is an integer between 1 and 4), growing with the moiré period but always fixed at integer multiples of n0.

It has been revealed that in Fig. 2e,f, the moiré period, determined from the carrier density of secondary Dirac points, exceeds in many samples the rigid-lattice limit of 14 nm (set by the 1.8% graphene–hBN lattice mismatch) and even reaches 17.7 nm, a consequence of the strain enhancement by mhBN and double alignment19,20 (Methods; Supplementary Information Section 4).

It has been revealed that by applying a large positive gate voltage above a certain threshold, a phase transition can be initiated: the moiré period remains unchanged but the samples become n-doped, again by an integer number of electrons per moiré plaquette, for both bottom-gated and dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c,d), and consistently across samples with different moiré sizes (Fig. 2e,f; Supplementary Information Section 3; Supplementary Figs. 5 and 6). Comprehensive control experiments (Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14; Supplementary Figs. 9–11 and 20–22) verify that this transition and the integer doping are intrinsic, excluding artefacts such as contamination. We emphasize that the integer doping is a direct observation requiring no fitting or registration procedure. As is well established for graphene superlattices5,6,7, the neutrality point–secondary Dirac point separation is fixed at four electrons per moiré unit cell. In Fig. 2c, the post-transition neutrality point (red) falls precisely at the midpoint between the pre-transition neutrality point and the secondary Dirac point (blue) and hence corresponds to exactly two electrons per moiré unit cell, as highlighted by the equally spaced ruler.

In a recent development, note that for the dual-gated samples (Fig. 2c), the gate voltage was applied simultaneously through top and bottom gates along the D = 0 line30 (dashed line in Fig. 3a). The switching depends only on the total carrier concentration and not on the displacement field (Supplementary Information Section 8; Supplementary Fig. 14). This mechanism fundamentally differs from recently reported two-dimensional ferroelectric systems, in which transitions occur through external electric-field-induced polarization changes26,31,32.

a–c, Vtg–Vbg maps of the transition process, each obtained by sweeping Vbg at stepped Vtg; a–c differ in gate sweep range and sweep history (marked by orange arrows). Orange arrows: sweep directions of top gate (Vtg) and back gate (Vbg). Blue and red arrows or solid lines represent Dirac points before and after transition, respectively. Numbers for blue lines and arrows give the doping per moiré unit cell at neutrality point (NP, 0), secondary Dirac points (SDP, ±4), tertiary Dirac points (TDP, ±8) and quaternary Dirac points (QDP, ±12); numbers for red lines and arrows are the same points offset by −2 electrons. Dashed lines indicate abrupt state changes at transition. The dashed black line in a denotes zero displacement field (D = 0), along which all transfer curves in Figs. 2 and 3 were performed; all forward and reverse transitions in a–c occur on this line, indicating that the displacement field is not the driving mechanism. In a–c, the transition point and the post-transition state are independent of gate range and sweep history. d, Continuous monitoring of the transition. Blue (5.3 V) and red (−6.9 V) dashed lines mark the critical voltages for transition and reversal, respectively. Black arrows track the measurement sequence (swp1–swp8); blue and red denote sweepings starting from the ‘before transition’ and ‘after transition’ states, respectively. Central dashed lines correspond to Δnint/n0 = 0, −4 (blue) and −2 and −6 (red). Shaded region above swp8 represents more than 100 repeated forward/reverse gate sweeps, after which the sample remains unchanged. e, Vdual D = 0–B maps, obtained through Vdual sweeps at fixed magnetic field steps. Orange arrows: sweep and field-variation directions (13 T to 0 T). The Vdual D = 0 sweep range surpasses the critical voltage of the forward transition (dashed blue line at 5.3 V) but not the reverse (dashed red line at −6.9 V) in d. Blue and red solid lines are states before and after transition, respectively. Notably, transition occurs at 3.8 T, at which magnetic length (approximately 13.4 nm) becomes commensurate with moiré periodicity. f,g, Zoom-in views of the blue and red boxed regions in d, respectively, revealing abrupt state changes at critical voltages (dashed lines). Circles represent the plotted resistance points; arrows indicate transition-induced resistance jump. h, Correlation between Rxx and Rxy; top axis, measured Hall density nfree; bottom axis, total gate-induced charge ntotal. The Hall zero-crossing (nfree = 0) occurs at ntotal = 2 holes per moiré cell, the difference being the localized charge nloc.

To investigate the transition dynamics and reproducibility, we conducted a series of Vtg–Vbg mappings and repeated switching tests (Rxx in Fig. 3; Rxy in Supplementary Fig. 24). Figure 3a–c reveals several Dirac points separated by intervals of four electrons per moiré plaquette5,6,7, marked with blue (before transition) or red (after transition) lines or arrows.

The phase transition occurs at Vtg = +3.9 V, Vbg = +5.3 V corresponding to ntotal = 3.75 × 1012 cm−2 along the D = 0 line in Fig. 3a. Following the transition, all features shift by two electrons per moiré plaquette. This shift throughout the entire superlattice spectrum clearly indicates that the moiré period is unchanged. The recovery occurs at Vtg = −5.0 V, Vbg = −6.9 V (corresponding to −4.85 × 1012 cm−2), also along the D = 0 line, restoring the entire gate dependence (Fig. 3b). Comparing Fig. 3c with Fig. 3a indicates that different Vtg–Vbg ranges and sweep protocols do not affect the transition characteristics: it occurs at identical gate points, as a single discrete event at the critical voltage rather than a continuous evolution.

In a recent development, figure 3d illustrates the transition dynamics through sequential measurements (swp1–swp8), with dashed lines at +5.3 V and −6.9 V marking the critical voltages for the forward and reverse transitions, respectively. Below the critical voltage, no transition occurs (swp1–swp2); on reaching it, the transition happens (swp3–swp4), at a critical voltage independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15; Supplementary Fig. 23). Similar behaviour is observed for the reverse transition (steps swp4–swp7). Figure 3f,g reveals zoomed-in views around the critical voltages for both the forward and reverse transitions. At the moment of transition, the resistance jumps from one state to another without any intermediate states, consistent with the abrupt translation of features observed in Vtg–Vbg mappings of Fig. 3a–c. Once the transition is induced, further increasing the gate voltage yields no continuous effect, indicating a saturation mechanism defined by the moiré unit cell capacity rather than the strength of the applied field. This behaviour differs markedly from that of ferroelectrics, for which polarization scales continuously with the applied field. The switching is fully reproducible: 100 consecutive cycles yield curves that overlap precisely (Fig. 3d, top). All behaviours discussed above support that the observed phase transition is a first-order-like transition (further information in Supplementary Information Section 43).

Recent findings suggest that notably, the transition can also be controlled by the magnetic field. Mapping the transition from 13 T down to 0 T (Fig. 3e) highlights that the transition is suppressed at high field, even for gate voltages far exceeding the critical value, and reappears at exactly the same critical voltage once the field drops below Bcrit = 3.8 T. The origin of this suppression remains to be established; we note, however, that the magnetic length at critical field \(\sqrt{\hbar /e{B}_{{\rm{crit}}}}\approx 13.4\,{\rm{nm}}\) is comparable with the moiré period for this sample of 13.8 nm.

In Fig. 3h, correlating Rxx with Rxy gives further information for theoretical analysis: the Hall-resistivity zero crossing (zero free carrier density nfree) occurs at a gate-induced density of two holes per moiré unit cell, the difference being compensated by localized electrons nloc.

To identify the origin of the phase transition, we consider the balance between elastic (strain) and van der Waals forces5,6, which can be modified through Coulomb interactions introduced by gate charging the graphene layer.

Sources indicate that using high-throughput density functional theory (DFT), we calculated the adhesion-energy distribution across the non-relaxed moiré plaquette, assuming perfect alignment of hBN on both sides, for the AB (Fig. 4a) and AA (Fig. 4b) relative configurations of the two hBN crystals (Supplementary Information Section 22; Supplementary Figs. 33–35). The relative energy of the two configurations can be compared by averaging the van der Waals potential over the entire moiré unit cell, as illustrated in Fig. 4c. The AB structure exhibits lower energy under neutral charging conditions (Fig. 4c–e). However, by assigning a negative charge on graphene above a certain threshold (corresponding to positive gate voltage applied) the AA configuration becomes more energetically favourable than AB (Fig. 4c,f,g), resulting in a structural phase transition from AB to AA.

It has been revealed that a,b, Schematics of the two configurations (AB (a) and AA (b)) and three high-symmetry stacking sites for both configurations. The red arrows on the left side indicate a shift of one of the hBN layers by one interatomic distance. c, Schematic diagram of the relative stability (in terms of the average adhesion energy taken over the entire moiré plaquette) of the two configurations as a function of doping. The solid lines represent the energy-favourable state. The crossing of the blue and red lines indicates the occurrence of the transition. Electron doping (positive gate) switches the relative stability between the two configurations and the consequent modification of the interlayer adhesion is proposed to be the driving force. d–g, Distribution of the interlayer adhesion energy (Eadh) across the moiré plaquette for the AB (d,f) and AA (e,g) configurations in the case of zero (d,e) and n-type (f,g) external doping (induced by gating in our experiments). The graphs in the middle give the corresponding adhesion energies of the three high-symmetry stackings as a function of interlayer distance between graphene and the top and bottom boron nitride layers near the equilibrium spacing (2.7–4.0 Å).

Sources indicate that the energy evolution with doping arises from gate-introduced Coulomb interactions, which enter the competition between van der Waals forces and elastic energies5,6. The balance among these three factors can be understood by comparing the relative stability of the AB and AA stacking configurations at high-symmetry points (Fig. 4a,b), which are the most representative sites and capture the qualitative trends under gating. Specifically, n-type doping substantially reduces the interlayer potential of AA-3 stacking: there, carbon atoms are vertically aligned with boron and the added electrons on carbon are strongly attracted to the positive charge on boron arising from the ionic nature of B–N bonds33. By contrast, the interlayer potential of AA-2 stacking is slightly elevated by the repulsion between the added electrons and the negatively charged nitrogen, whereas AA-1 and all three high-symmetry sites of the AB alignment remain almost unchanged, as the interaction of added electrons with boron is compensated by their interaction with nitrogen. This picture is substantiated by DFT calculations (Fig. 4d–g; Supplementary Information Sections 22–27). We can generalize the similar gate-induced phase transitions to other systems in which at least one of the multiply aligned layers has electropolarity (Supplementary Information Section 37).

We now turn to the origin of the integer doping in graphene, which we attribute to strain-induced PLLs localized at the vertices of the reconstructed moiré domains. The reconstructed phases for AB and AA configurations are directly visualized through STM measurements (STM images of different regions, and of a reference single-aligned graphene/hBN region on the same flake, are shown in Supplementary Figs. 12 and 13) and theoretically simulated by MD calculations (Fig. 5a,b). On the basis of the atomic displacements calculated by MD, we obtained the strain distribution in the reconstructed moiré unit cell (schematics shown in Fig. 5c,d), as well as the associated pseudomagnetic field7,8,9,10,11,34 (left panels of Fig. 5e,f) (Supplementary Information Sections 24, 29 and 31).

In a recent development, the reconstruction results in distinct strain fields for the AB and AA configurations (Fig. 5c,d). For the AB configuration, it is the AB-1 and AB-3 stackings that have much lower energy than AB-2 (Fig. 4d,f), so the reconstruction forms triangular domains of AB-1 and AB-3 stackings, accompanied by notable strain and out-of-plane corrugation at the AB-2 stacking (Fig. 5c). By contrast, for the AA configuration, it is the AA-3 stacking that has the lowest energy (Fig. 4e,g), leading to hexagonally reconstructed AA-3 moiré domain, with the strain concentrated at AA-2 and AA-1 stacked corners of the moiré plaquette (Fig. 5d). Here the predominance of in-plane strain in AA (versus out-of-plane corrugation in AB) originates from the mirror symmetry of the AA configuration, which yields negligible net out-of-plane force (Supplementary Information Section 38; Supplementary Fig. 54). In both cases, the strain results in strong PMF.

In a recent development, the effect of this strong reconstruction on the band structure involves two ingredients: (1) the PMF and (2) variations of the local work function across the moiré plaquette35. We first calculated the band structure for the reconstructed AB and AA configurations, excluding the variations in work function (Fig. 5g,i). Two features emerge: (1) a substantial bandgap is opened owing to the reconstruction-induced difference between the on-site potential of each carbon sublattice35,36,37; (2) several fourfold spin-valley degenerate flat bands appear within the bandgap (Supplementary Information Sections 29, 31 and 32). Plotting the corresponding real-space wavefunctions (inset colour maps in Fig. 5g,i) reveals their localization at the vertices of the moiré domain AB-2, AA-1 and AA-2, in which strain and the PMF both peak. These flat bands can be interpreted as PLLs arising from the PMF. In reciprocal space, they are manifested as flat bands that host strongly localized electrons25. Equivalently, we can view them as strain-induced quantum dots situated at the moiré-domain vertices. Notably, because the zeroth PLL in graphene sits at the NP and is only half-filled, it cannot change the doping level unless its energy is shifted and hybridizes with either the valence or the conduction dispersive bands.

Recent findings suggest that taking into account the work-function landscape across the moiré plaquette (owing to local strain and van der Waals environment) shifts the flat bands away from the bandgap, hybridizing them with either the valence or the conduction bands and thus resulting in doping of graphene. The curvature at the AB-2 site lowers the hybridization of the pz orbital of carbons (similar to carbon nanotubes38), increases the local work function at AB-2 and consequently shifts its corresponding flat band downward (Fig. 5h). Conversely, the in-plane strain at AA-1 and AA-2 vertices reduces the carbon–carbon distance, resulting in the reduction of the local work function and upward shift of the corresponding flat bands39 (Fig. 5j). Other factors, such as the van der Waals environment, contribute with the same trend35,37 (Supplementary Information Section 27; Supplementary Figs. 43–45).

The resulting work-function variation lowers the flat bands towards the valence band in the AB configuration and raises them towards the conduction band in AA (Fig. 5h,j). Once the empty/filled flat bands in the AB/AA configuration cross the valence/conduction band, the holes/electrons trapped in the corresponding quantum dots are released into the body of the moiré domain and start to contribute to transport. This shifts the Fermi level away from the neutrality point to the valence/conduction bands and the AB/AA configuration will demonstrate p-doping/n-doping, respectively. In this picture, electrons are redistributed between the conductive moiré domain and the insulating quantum dots at its vertices.

Hole-side angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements corroborate this picture. Comparing the mhBN/graphene/hBN heterostructure against a conventional graphene/hBN reference region on the same flake (Fig. 5k,l), a flat band (orange) appears exclusively in the mhBN region and hybridizes with the neighbouring dispersive band (red), consistent with our above picture.

Industry observers note that such a doping mechanism explains the observed integer charging per moiré plaquette. In the simplest picture, each PLL holds g = gsgv = 4 states (spin × valley degeneracy). In the AB configuration (Fig. 5e), this condition is met at only one vertex per plaquette. Because the zero-energy PLL is initially half-filled, each vertex accommodates two more electrons (or holes), giving n/n0 = +2 for the initial p-doped state (blue sweep in Fig. 2d); in the AA configuration, two vertices contribute, giving n/n0 = −4 (red sweep). This accounts for the p-doping before the transition being consistently smaller than the n-doping after it.

Building on the above simplest picture, understanding such integer quantization also requires fundamental energy balance considerations. A well-established physical principle for structural stabilization seen in phenomena ranging from the Peierls transition in one-dimensional crystals to the filled shells of noble gases is as follows: when energy spectra are discrete, configurations with fully occupied and fully empty states separated by a gap become energetically favoured. In our system, the necessary discrete spectrum arises not from atomic orbitals or external magnetic fields but from PLLs generated by the strong periodic strain of the moiré reconstruction. Crucially, this solid-state system has a tunability absent in atomic prototypes: it can tune the electrostatic energy directly by solid gate and self-optimize the energy spectrum to maintain integer fillings. Similar to flux optimization in GaAs quantum rings40, the system can adjust the PMF strength (through strain redistribution) to ensure that the PLL degeneracy exactly matches the electron occupancy. The finite energy gain from fully occupying a Landau level compensates for the extra elastic deformation costs, effectively locking the system into a stable, integer-quantized state. We note that this self-optimization operates at the local scale involving only small strain variations around moiré vertices. This local self-optimization is distinct from the global structural transition itself, which is driven by the competition between van der Waals, elastic and electrostatic energies (Fig. 4).

Further evidence identifying commensurate filling of the discrete PLL spectrum as the origin of the integer doping, and ruling out alternative scenarios (charge trapping, Coulomb blockade of moiré-potential quantum dots, interfacial ferroelectricity and contact electrostatics), is provided in Supplementary Information Section 39.

We believe that our work opens a upcoming avenue for engineering structural and electronic phase transition in dynamical van der Waals systems through careful balancing of Coulomb, van der Waals and elastic energy contributions. Structures with several aligned interfaces can result in more complex phase transitions and electronic states. We also point out that the periodic arrangement of localized PLLs demonstrated here constitutes a regularly distributed array of quantum dots defined by strain. This connection to quantum dot physics opens avenues for further fundamental and applied investigations. Notably, such integer doping and phase transition occur across a broad range of moiré sizes (from 6 nm to 17.7 nm), eliminating the requirement for precise twist angle control in sample fabrication.

Sources indicate that heterostructures were assembled using the standard dry-transfer technique. Two device architectures were used: dual-gated hBN/graphene/mhBN/hBN, in which the mhBN–hBN interface was intentionally misaligned by 15° to ensure superlubricity, and bottom-gated mhBN/graphene/hBN. Seven more types of reference device were fabricated by the same process (full list and data in Supplementary Information Section 4). The sample types are categorized by alignment and hBN thickness. The alignment scenarios include double alignment (a), single alignment (b), top and bottom hBN aligned with each other but not with the encapsulated graphene (c), single alignment with unencapsulated graphene (d) and a nonaligned three-layer stack (e). Samples with the same alignment are further subdivided by hBN thickness (bulk, bilayer and monolayer hBN), as illustrated in the schematics in Supplementary Fig. 7, into a1–a4, b1, b2, c1, d1 and e1. The a2 and a4 samples are the devices used in Fig. 2, listed in Supplementary Tables 1 (samples 1–8) and 2 (samples 9–10). Other sample types are for reference with data in Supplementary Information Section 4.

For the non-capped (single-gated) samples, simultaneous alignment of graphene to both hBN crystals was confirmed by AFM and transport measurements: the Fourier transform of the AFM topography (inset of Fig. 2b) shows two moiré periodicities of 10.8 nm and 12.0 nm (ref. 19), corroborated by the two sets of secondary Dirac points in the transfer curves13,14,15,41 (Fig. 2d). For the dual-gated encapsulated samples, in which the two moiré patterns are practically identical in size and the secondary Dirac points coincide in gate voltage, double alignment was confirmed primarily by Raman spectroscopy combined with optical imaging and AFM (ref. 42). Detailed analysis is given in Supplementary Information Section 2. The thickness of the hBN layers (down to monolayer) was confirmed by Raman and AFM measurements (Supplementary Information Section 2).

It has been revealed that transport measurements were performed in a TeslatronPT cryostat at a base temperature of T = 1.6 K, equipped with a superconducting magnet providing fields up to 14 T. Longitudinal and Hall resistances were measured in a four-terminal configuration using standard low-frequency lock-in SR860 lock-in amplifiers, with an AC excitation current of 5 nA at 37 Hz to avoid sample heating. Gate voltages were applied by a Keithley 2601 source meter. For dual-gated devices, the top-gate and back-gate voltages were swept simultaneously along the D = 0 line30 unless stated otherwise. The critical transition voltage is independent of the gate sweep rate (Supplementary Information Section 15); control experiments excluding contamination and other artefacts are detailed in Supplementary Information Sections 5 and 14.

It has been revealed that the stability, work function, electronic structures and charge transfer of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures have been thoroughly studied using DFT calculations. Our calculations are based on the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional as implemented in the Vienna Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP). The interaction between the valence electrons and ionic cores is described within the projector augmented-wave approach with a plane-wave energy cut-off of 500 eV. The widely used semi-local approximations for the exchange-correlation energy do not take long-range correlations into account correctly. Thus, they fail to reproduce van der Waals attraction and the prediction of equilibrium geometries of van der Waals bound layered systems. To address the problem, the dispersion correction schemes proposed by Grimme were used to treat the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN layers. The Brillouin zone was sampled with the Monkhorst–Pack grid and the grid sizes depend on the size of the supercells used. The grid was chosen to be as dense as 31 × 31 × 1 for a primitive cell and Γ-point only for a large supercell of near 5 nm. The vacuum space of at least 15 Å was used to avoid interaction between neighbouring layers. In the structural energy minimization, the atomic coordinates are allowed to relax until the forces on all of the atoms are less than 0.01 eV Å−1. The energy tolerance is 10−6 eV.

Industry observers note that because full-scale DFT calculation would be computationally unrealistic for a moiré unit cell consisting of 56 × 56 atoms of graphene monolayer and at least twice the 55 × 55 atoms of two hBN layers, we would investigate the structure using a combination of DFT calculations and empirical potentials MD simulations. For specified stacking of the hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, calculations were done using the commensurate structure with the graphene lattice. To understand the adhesion energy and the work function distribution of the moiré structure, we screen the local stacking of the moiré cell of hBN/graphene/hBN using a 21 × 21 grid of sampling points. The structure at each sampling point was obtained by shifting the graphene with respect to the hBN layers on the two sides. To model the gate-induced electron doping in graphene, extra electrons were added to the supercell and a uniform positive charge background was added to compensate and ensure the charge neutrality of the system.

The structure relaxations were implemented in the Large-scale Atomic/Molecular Massively Parallel Simulator (LAMMPS). We used many-body Tersoff potentials to treat the in-plane C–C and B–N interactions. The interlayer van der Waals interaction between the graphene and hBN was described by the registry-dependent Kolmogorov–Crespi potential. To model the interlayer interaction between graphene and hBN under gating, we vary the strength of the C–B interaction relative to the C–N interaction using a scaling parameter (s). We found that, for s = 5% and s = 50%, the potential is qualitatively consistent with the DFT interlayer adhesion of the trilayer heterostructure in the absence and presence of doping, respectively. Using the s = 50% scaling of the C–B/C–N interaction, we successfully simulated the structural transition of the heterostructure. To include the substrate effect of bulk hBN and model the interlayer interactions among different boron nitride layers, we proposed a Lennard–Jones 6–12 potential to describe the repulsive and attractive terms, and Coulomb’s law is used for the electrostatic interactions. This yields.

in which ϵij and σij are the potential parameters to control the strength of the attractive and repulsive interactions, respectively, rij is the interaction distance between atom i and atom j, qi and qj are the atomic partial charge in units of the elementary charge and Kc is the coulombic constant. We set 0.2 and −0.2 for the B and N, respectively after careful evaluation. Because of the smaller van der Waals radius of B (about 1.92 Å) and large interlayer distance of hBN layers (about 3.30 Å), we neglected the short-range B–B interactions in this study. ϵBN and ϵNN were set to 0.3035 and 10.8237 meV, respectively. Also, we used 3.75 and 3.1461 Å for σBN and σNN, respectively. During the simulation, the cut-off distance was set to 8 Å for the attractive and repulsive terms. A long-range solver of the standard coulombic Ewald summations was used to compute long-range coulombic interactions or long-range interactions. The atomic structures were equilibrated using the NVT ensemble (canonical ensemble). A 2.0-ns annealing process from 300 K to 1 K was first carried out and then the other 0.5-ns timescale was implemented to stabilize the structures. A time step of 1.0 fs was used and the relaxation was completed when the forces are less than 10−6 eV Å−1. The unrotated heterostructures were modelled by 56 × 56 unit cells of graphene and 55 × 55 unit cells of hBN, resulting in a 1.8% mismatch in lattice constant. We used four monolayers of hBN to imitate bulk substrate, in which the bottom two layers were fixed and the top two layers allowed relaxation during the MD simulations.

The lattice structures of graphene and hBN are incommensurate; although both feature a honeycomb lattice (graphene of carbon atoms and hBN of boron and nitrogen atoms), the hBN lattice period is δ ≈ 1.8%, longer than that of graphene, a = 0.246 nm. Including an anticlockwise twist of the hBN layer, θ, the interference of the two lattice potentials at the interface gives a moiré superlattice, magnified from the graphene lattice, with moiré superlattice period \(\lambda \approx a/\sqrt{{\delta }^{2}+{\theta }^{2}}\), and rotated by φ ≈ −arctan(θ/δ). The moiré superlattice Bragg vectors are constructed as linear combinations of the ‘first star’ of non-zero vectors, Gm ≈ δ · gm − θ(ez × gm) m = (0, 1,…, 5), expressed in terms of the first star of graphene vectors, \({{\bf{g}}}_{{\rm{m}}}=\frac{4\pi }{\sqrt{3}a}\left(-\sin \frac{m2\pi }{3},\cos \frac{m2\pi }{3}\right)\), and depicted alongside the moiré Brillouin zone.

In a recent development, though, we'd be genuinely shocked if Liverpool was his ultimate destination. The Red part of it, anyway. Tanaka is now 28 and not really of the kind of quality that the Reds would ignore his age to get a deal done.

There's no long-term investment here, in other words, and the short-term wouldn't be good enough to justify a fee. Really the only players in that age bracket that Liverpool have signed within the past 10 years are Wataru Endo and Thiago.

Both were special cases. Endo was needed because the squad lacked a specialist defensive midfielder at a time when Liverpool really needed one. And Thiago was needed because he was Thiago.

Tanaka ticks neither box. If he were completely free, things would change but there's no chance Liverpool are considering potential free transfers in 2028. Instead, we imagine this is actually agents driving up interest to get Leeds moving on a contract.

Arsenal 1-0 Hull: Not efficient, but enough

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points.
  • Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play.
  • It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In yesterday’s preview blog, I spoke about Arsenal’s attacking efficiency, and how that might be key to taking all three points. In yesterday’s game against Hull, Arsenal took 21 shots, 10 of which were on target, and scored one goal from that. Efficient?

Despite generally dominating possession, I thought there was a lack of precision in certain aspects of our first half play. Passes weren’t quite quick enough or accurate enough, but there were moments when we could have found the breakthrough. Gabriel almost got on the end of a Noni Madueke cross which was flicked on towards the back post, Rice had a tame shot from a free kick before a late header which he probably should have done better with.

And then there was Kai Havertz. It’s fair to say Hull didn’t leave a lot of room behind a defensive line that often had six players stretched across it, but late in the half a superb Martin Odegaard pass sent him clean through, one on one with the keeper. I haven’t seen replays but in real time I felt like he should have pulled the trigger – instead he over-complicated it. You have to be prepared to shoot from there, even if it’s on your wrong foot.

Recent findings suggest that then there was a penalty incident when he complained vociferously, play went on, the ref was then told to go to the screen and we all assumed it would be a penalty. However, the ref said it was a foul but Havertz was offside – and it felt like a massive waste of time. Afterwards, it emerged it should have been a penalty, but apparently the rule is ‘open to interpretation’. So clear as mud then.

In the second half, we seemed to play down our right a lot, with Madueke the outlet most of the time. I thought he did pretty well, much better than Christos Tzolis on the other side, but the breakthrough wouldn’t come. Mikel Merino replaced Rice (who seemed to be on the end of a wild challenge in midfield that the ref just ignored as he tumbled through the air), and Viktor Gyokeres came on for Havertz.

On 71 minutes though, we found the goal. Madueke’s shot was spilled by the keeper, Odegaard was quickest to react to poke the ball home for 1-0. And to be fair, you always felt confident that would be enough. We are the masters of the single goal margin win, and this was another one. Not a day that will live long in the memory or anything, but a 1-0 win that takes us into the Interlull in really good shape, and there’s not much arguing with that.

Sources indicate that or really, much more to say about this game. Mikel Arteta sounded happy enough, saying:.

Sources indicate that I’m delighted with the win. To go into the international break with a win is one of the best things about being a coach or player, I would say. Regarding the performance, I thought we were the better team, had enough chances to score and make it bigger for ourselves and we weren’t efficient enough to take them.

We then had to rely on generating volume, plenty of persisting until we finally broke them down. Martin then got the goal. Not the most beautiful one, but the most effective one, a simple ‘shoot and then follow the next action’, and that was ultimately enough to win the game.

Recent findings suggest that so Arsenal sit top of the table, with 9 wins from 10 so far this season in the league, and it’s a very impressive run of form. Do I wish we had more attacking potency? Absolutely, and I do worry a bit that it might bite us in the arse somewhere down the line, but for now, we can see that this is a team that just knows how to win, and perhaps that’s the most important thing.

Recent findings suggest that right, I’m gonna leave it there for this morning. I have to head back to Dublin today. It was great to see lots of you over the weekend, until next time! And we’ll have an Arsecast Extra for you tomorrow too.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

Industry observers note that what they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously remarked of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”.

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

It has been revealed that defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

According to recent reports, that is unacceptable and is their fewest number of league victories in a top-flight campaign since 1986-87. Back then they sacked their manager in November and brought in a certain Alex Ferguson.

It has been revealed that the hard truth is Carrick needs to start collecting some “Ws” in those results columns. United are already 14 points behind leaders Manchester City and five outside the probable Champions League places. Qualifying again for that tournament must be the minimum expectation.

Industry observers note that ruben Amorim, Carrick’s predecessor, lost his job within 24 hours of the same 1-1 scoreline at Elland Road last season – dismissed after Martínez-like explosive comments again aimed at director of football Jason Wilcox. Carrick will not suffer the same fate after this, but the ice is becoming increasingly thin.

Recent findings suggest that we have seen this movie before at United. A slow start to the season, a period of drift, falling out of contention, no reaction on the pitch, backing from the hierarchy that becomes increasingly unconvincing. And then a change.

Industry observers note that can Carrick, who genuinely does still retain support at the highest level, alter that pattern? Does he have it in him? Is he too passive like his team? Carrick noted this draw felt like a “fresh start”, but on this evidence that comment can be classified as wildly optimistic.

In a recent development, having directed his criticism at the United hierarchy, and specifically Wilcox, the former Leeds winger who was here, over a lack of summer signings, Martínez apologised and was named in the starting XI. But the Argentine only lasted to half-time, withdrawn injured with a tight thigh, and sat watching the second half with his hood up over his head.

What United did sign in the last window was three midfielders – at a cost of £155m – and all three started: Carlos Baleba alongside Andrey Santos with Youri Tielemans in the No 10 role, which meant Bruno Fernandes was pushed out to the left, from where he constantly wanted to come in-field, with Amad Diallo on the right.

According to recent reports, carrick talked of having a “fresh spine” as well as that fresh start. But it did not make for a potent combination even if, further forward, Bryan Mbeumo played through the middle and scored one. He should have scored another.

Bryan Mbeumo finds the net this time to put Manchester United 1-0 up at Leeds! 🔴 https://t.co/NKDIhlUND1.

Recent findings suggest that but beyond that United created little. “It was a dominant performance against Man United,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, claimed. He was right. If one team deserved to win it was his. They had the chances but snatched at them with Anton Stach, in injury time, having a weak shot cleared off the line by Martínez’s replacement Noussair Mazraoui after a mistake by goalkeeper Senne Lammens. Stach had to score.

Industry observers note that united were ahead at half-time. Mbeumo had headed wastefully wide when unmarked but did well to force his way past James Justin and meet a low cross from Tielemans to poke the ball home. The way the usually undemonstrative Carrick punched the air in his technical area revealed the pressure he felt. It was something to build on. To gain control.

In a recent development, leeds had started well but did not really pose much of a threat – beyond forcing Lammens to save well from Nico Elvedi’s downward header – and maybe the earlier kick-off subdued the crowd. This was far from a bear pit.

But after the break, Leeds were comfortably the better side. The nature of their equalising goal, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin too strong and alert for first Baleba and then Mbeumo to fire in from a corner, exposed the enduring softness at the heart of United.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalises for Leeds against Manchester United 👊 https://t.co/mnpyxZJKbm.

In a recent development, and that must be addressed by Carrick, especially as he appeared to sacrifice attacking intent by shoring up defensively. But that duvet is looking far too inadequate right now. Or Carrick is making it appear so.

Michael Carrick says he has put on “the headphones” this week in an effort to drown out the noise, but admitted Manchester United have to stop their struggles from snowballing.

United sit just two points above the relegation zone after a 1-1 draw at Leeds left them with just one win from their opening seven Premier League matches.

Carrick claimed the result felt like a “fresh start” after a week in which Lisandro Martínez publicly apologised for criticising Jason Wilcox, the United director of football, and the Old Trafford board.

But the United manager acknowledged their position “doesn’t look too good” and that they must start winning soon to stop the club from entering another doom cycle.

“Listen, we’re not accepting it as everything’s great by any stretch, so I’m realistic with that,” said the United manager, who claimed “the headphones have been on this week”.

“But sometimes you do struggle, sometimes there’s a bit of it where you have to find a way through it. We haven’t really had to go through that yet [before now] and we have to find a way through it.

Industry observers note that “There has been a cycle at times here over a period of time when it can go in different directions. We’ve got to be stable enough to keep doing the right things for the right reasons as a group, and we’re more than capable of winning football matches.

“I understand the situation doesn’t look too good if you look at it from a certain way, but I’ve no doubts we can go on a good run.”.

United face Como in the Champions League in Italy on Wednesday before Bournemouth visit Old Trafford four days later.

According to recent reports, carrick said he remains convinced United can still have a strong campaign, despite their worst start to a season for 40 years. I know what we’ve got in the changing room, where we want to get to, how we want to get there,” he said. “We know we can do it.

“We’ve done it for some time, and we feel we’re a better group now, and I do feel that. Sometimes it doesn’t always show, but you get a feeling and I’m encouraged by a lot of things. And if we keep doing the right things, I think we can still have a really good season.”.

Asked if he would be putting the headphones back on this week ahead of two more pivotal games, Carrick added: “Nah, it’s always quiet for me.”.

Industry observers note that martínez was substituted at half-time at Elland Road with a tight thigh just days after his tirade at club executives and Marcus Rashford was left out for “purely tactical” reasons. “Nothing personal, the front players were doing a good job on and off the ball,” Carrick said. “Everyone is ready for Wednesday.”.

The Leeds boss told Sky Sports: “We are slightly disappointed it is just a point. Overall, I felt it was not necessary to be losing at half time but it is still Manchester United. Second half, we got the equaliser, we should have kept up the dominance, too many strikes went over the crossbar but it was overall a solid performance. We should have won the game but we move on.

Recent findings suggest that “We took it as a compliment that we have done many things right over the last month if we were seen as favourites against Manchester Untiedbut we have earned this. We wanted to prove the comments right.

“We were the dominant side but we couldn’t capitalise as we lacked quality in and around the box.

“It notes a lot about how much respect we have earned. Overall, this is where we are at the moment and overall, it is a good place to be.

According to recent reports, “It is still difficult in this league to win points. You have to be clinical and be very, very effective but we have to keep going.”.

It has been revealed that speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “I think we could’ve played with a bit more quality in the final third, particularly in the first half. We were getting good quality in the box but just not enough numbers.

In a recent development, “We made sure in the second half we came out with more confidence going forward. I think we were unlucky not to win the game.

It has been revealed that “They tried to [match us up formation-wise]. Not surprised given what happened last season. They were probably looking at our physical output and the way we liked to play and tried to go man-for-man.

“It took us a little bit to adjust to it, but I don’t think it was too difficult to adjust. It was more down to us and maybe a lack of quality in the final third.”.

Just 10 months on from Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United, the club return to Elland Road on Sunday afternoon with another manager under pressure and the director of football again in the spotlight.

The difference is Michael Carrick still has a chance to determine the course of his United future whereas Amorim had already sealed his fate after a furious bust-up with Jason Wilcox 48 hours before his last game ended in a 1-1 draw with Leeds and post-match fireworks.

But even for a club never far from a crisis, it seems remarkable to think they are back in a tailspin so soon after Amorim’s sacking in early January.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League fixture between Manchester United and Leeds United at Elland Road.

Carrick is under immense pressure to get a result here in Yorkshire, with last weekend’s 1-1 draw with 10-man Tottenham at Old Trafford condemning Man Utd to their worst league start for 40 years.

Leeds are eighth and the club will be harbouring ambitions of a top-half finish in the Premier League for the first time since the 2019/20 season, with the prospect of qualifying for European football not out of the realm of possibility.

In a recent development, unlike Man Utd, Leeds have a settled, reliable system that clearly suits their current squad. Elland Road will also be a cauldron of hostility and noise, given the fierce backdrop between these two bitter rivals.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.
  • The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 20 Nov 2026 22:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 01:26.

Fulham goalkeeper Benjamin Lecomte will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with an Achilles injury.

The Frenchman sustained the injury in a behind-closed-doors game against West Ham United during the international break.

Revealing the extent of the injury, Alvaro Arbeloa told reporters on Friday: "Unfortunately, Lecomte injured his Achilles tendon against West Ham, so he will be out for the rest of the season.

“We are sorry for him because he is very notable and it was very sad.”.

Lecomte has not played in the Premier League this season, but he featured in three of Fulham’s EFL Cup games, including a 1-0 defeat to Crystal Palace last month.

As a result of Lecomte’s injury, Alex Borto and Dino Kaiser will be the backup options for the club’s undisputed first-choice goalkeeper Bernd Leno.

Arbeloa also revealed Emile Smith Rowe is unlikely to be fit for Saturday’s lunchtime kick-off against Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium.

“Smith Rowe has some pain in his hip, so I think he won't be available for tomorrow.

“I think it’s nothing serious - some pain and discomfort, so we will see next week, but it doesn't look really serious.”.

The news of Smith Rowe's physical issue represents the latest setback in what is proving to be a difficult campaign for the Arsenal academy product.

The 28-year-old made 37 Premier League appearances in Marco Silva's final season in charge, but he has featured in just four league games under Arbeloa due to injury and selection decisions.

In more positive news, Arbeloa explained that Tom Cairney could be in contention to return to the squad after missing the draw against Newcastle United before the international window.

If available, Cairney could have a role to play off the bench as Fulham look to end their woeful run of form against Manchester City.

The Cottagers have lost each of their last 17 Premier League games against the Citizens since they played out a 2-2 draw at Craven Cottage in September 2011.

Meanwhile, their last head-to-head victory took place in April 2009 when Clinton Dempsey netted a brace in a 3-1 win at the Etihad Stadium.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career.
  • Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, I watched Man Utd v Aston Villa last night. When Villa conceded late on to let a two goal lead slip for the second time in the game, Unai Emery threw a strop and went down the tunnel. It’s not the first time he’s eschewed a handshake with the opposition manager, and his post-game interview where he insisted he thought the game was over was very funny because it was such obvious bullshit.

Recent findings suggest that this is someone who has managed over 1000 games in his career. I’m pretty sure he knows when the final whistle blows and when it doesn’t. Can you imagine if Mikel Arteta did that? You wouldn’t be able to move for all the opinion pieces about what a sore loser he is and all the rest. But perhaps Emery gets a pass because he is ‘the best manager in the league’. Anyway, perhaps it provides a stay of execution for Michael Carrick at Man Utd, which can only be a good thing.

Meanwhile, it looks as if Pierre Sage is gonna get fired by Crystal Palace and replaced by Thomas Frank. That seems a sensible appointment to me. Enough time has passed since his spell at Sp*rs for the toxins to wear off, and he’s clearly a good manager. I’ve never been convinced by Sage, I just think he looks too scruffy. As if someone got a 10 year old to draw man and brought it to life.

I quite enjoyed this quote from Mikel Arteta in his post-game press conference after Saturday’s 1-0 win over Hull:.

Sometimes we try to score the perfect goal against low blocks, but we need to be much more chaotic than that. If we open the scoring much earlier also, it changes the game.

In a recent development, I love it as a concept, adding some chaos to our control makes a lot of sense, but it also kinda seems at odds with what the manager asks of his players. Maybe he just means more shots from distance, maybe riskier pass when we’re trying to break the opposition down, or maybe there’s something he’s got cooking for over the Interlull and when we return we see something we never expected. He did kick the shit out of a dugout chair on Saturday, that’s a latest enough development to be fair.

It has been revealed that I wonder was he referring to the Kai Havertz chance in the first half, when he could have shot on his right foot but tried to cut back/lay it off. If you shoot, maybe you don’t score but as we saw with the winning goal from Martin Odegaard, it might end up in the path of another Arsenal player who can finish it off. Perhaps too there’s a bit of a through line between being more chaotic and what Noni Madueke is doing at the moment. He can be a bit scattergun, but as Nick Wright points out on Sky Sports, his numbers are improving. I don’t think Arteta will ever embrace full chaos, all the time, but if he can add a little more to the mix, it could certainly help.

Right, I have to leave it there for this morning. A bit shorter than normal, I know. We will have an Arsecast Extra for you a bit later on though. We’ve already put out the call for questions on BlueSky @gunnerblog.bsky.social and @arseblog.com, so fire away using the hashtag #arsecastextra – or if you’re an Arseblog Member on Patreon, leave your question in the #arsecast-extra-questions channel on our Discord server.

In a recent development, the pod should be out around around lunchtime. Until then, have a good one.
